title: Anthropic files S-1 paperwork for blockbuster AI IPO
description: Anthropic filed its S-1 with the SEC, reporting about $16.3 billion in first-half 2026 revenue against $1.2 billion a year earlier. Press coverage of the filing puts the net loss at $80.7 billion, largely from non-cash charges tied to convertible notes. The company plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

title: Anthropic's S-1, by the numbers: A thriving business—with a $498 billion asterisk
description: Fortune breaks down the financials in Anthropic's IPO filing, including adjusted operating profit in the first half and first-ever positive operating cash flow. The filing also warns that revenue is not expected to keep growing at comparable rates.

title: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals where OpenAI could have the upper hand
description: Fortune analyzes what Anthropic's S-1 discloses about its competitive position relative to OpenAI. The piece looks at areas where OpenAI may hold an advantage as both labs compete for enterprise customers.

title: Meta launches plan for $95 billion stock offering to fund AI expansion
description: Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion in stock, starting with about $35 billion in underwritten offerings and followed by an at-the-market program. The money is meant to fund AI infrastructure and superintelligence efforts, including multi-gigawatt data center campuses. Meta's 2026 capex guidance stands at $135 billion to $145 billion.

title: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership
description: Nvidia and AMD said they will invest $3 billion and $1 billion respectively in Meta's share offering. The investments deepen the chipmakers' ties to Meta as it expands its AI infrastructure buildout.

title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as AI leads to efficiency push
description: Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees, roughly 27% of its workforce, in the US, Canada, India and the UK. The company ties the move to cost control during heavy AI infrastructure spending, and employees must decide in early December.
